items.name: Repair Windows system files
items.summary: For crashes, errors about missing files, or Windows features that stopped working. Checks Windows' own files and replaces damaged ones.
items.effect: Only damaged Windows files are replaced. It can take a long time and may ask for a restart. If SFC says it could not repair some files, details are in C:\Windows\Logs\CBS\CBS.log.
sources: Microsoft Support: System File Checker (DISM first, then SFC)

options.label: Create a restore point first
options.detail: Windows allows one automatic restore point a day, so this may be skipped.

options.label: Also clean up old update files afterwards
options.detail: Frees some space; old updates can no longer be uninstalled.

steps.title: Create a restore point
args: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; Checkpoint-Computer -Description 'TidyWindow: before repairing Windows files' -RestorePointType MODIFY_SETTINGS; 'Restore point created.'

items.name: Reset Windows Update
items.summary: For updates that fail, get stuck downloading, or never finish checking. Stops the update services, clears what they downloaded, and starts them again.
items.effect: Downloaded update files are renamed to .bak (Windows downloads them again). Your installed updates are not removed. Afterwards open Settings > Windows Update and check for updates.
sources: Microsoft Learn: Reset Windows Update components manually
WinUtil (cross-check; its policy clean-up was not copied)

options.label: Also reset the update database and certificate store
options.detail: Use only if the first try did not help. The list of past updates in Settings starts empty.

steps.title: Remove the old download queue files
Set aside the downloaded update files
Set aside the update certificate store

items.name: Check the drive for errors
items.summary: For slow or freezing PCs, files that will not open, or strange crashes. Reads the health of your drives and scans the system drive for problems.
items.effect: Nothing is changed; this only reads and reports. If errors are reported, open an administrator Command Prompt and run chkdsk C: /f; Windows repairs the drive at the next restart.
sources: Microsoft Learn: Repair-Volume -Scan (an online scan that changes nothing)

steps.title: Read drive health
args: Get-PhysicalDisk | Select-Object FriendlyName, MediaType, HealthStatus, OperationalStatus | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String -Width 120

steps.title: Scan the system drive
args: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; try { 'Scanning the drive. Windows shows no progress for this, so expect a quiet minute or two.'; $result = Repair-Volume -DriveLetter $env:SystemDrive.Substring(0, 1) -Scan; "Result: $result"; if ($result -ne 'NoErrorsFound') { exit 1 } } catch { $_.Exception.Message; exit 2 }

items.name: Create a restore point
items.summary: A save point to go back to if something goes wrong after a change. Good to do before repairs or installing drivers.
items.effect: Uses a little disk space. System Protection must be on for your system drive, and Windows allows one automatic restore point a day, so it may be skipped.

steps.title: Create the restore point
args: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; Checkpoint-Computer -Description 'TidyWindow restore point' -RestorePointType MODIFY_SETTINGS; 'Restore point created.'

items.name: Fix the clock
items.summary: For a clock that is a few minutes off, which also causes website certificate errors and sign-in problems. Starts the time service and asks the internet to set the time.
items.effect: Only the time is corrected. The time zone is not changed; set it in Settings > Time & language if it is wrong.

steps.title: Set the time from the internet

items.name: Rebuild the search index
items.summary: For Windows search that finds nothing, shows old files, or uses a lot of the disk. Deletes the search database so Windows builds a fresh one.
items.effect: Search results are incomplete while Windows re-indexes, which can take from a few minutes to over an hour and is quicker when you leave the PC alone.
items.duration: A minute, then Windows indexes in the background
sources: Microsoft Q&A: Windows Search troubleshooting (delete Windows.edb)

items.name: Update Defender and run a quick scan
items.summary: Gets the latest virus definitions and scans the places malware usually hides.
items.effect: Nothing is removed without Defender's own decision. Does not work if another antivirus has turned Microsoft Defender off.

steps.title: Run a quick scan
args: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; Start-MpScan -ScanType QuickScan; 'Quick scan finished.'; Get-MpThreat | Select-Object ThreatName, IsActive | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String -Width 120

items.name: Refresh the network connection
items.summary: For websites that will not load while others work, or after switching networks. Clears the saved addresses Windows remembers and optionally asks the router for a new one.
items.effect: Your connection may drop for a few seconds. Nothing is reset to defaults, so settings such as a fixed IP address are kept.
sources: Microsoft Support: Fix network connection issues

options.label: Ask the router for a new IP address
options.detail: The usual fix for “connected, no internet”.

options.label: Restart the network adapters
options.detail: Disconnects Wi-Fi and Ethernet for a few seconds.

items.name: Reset the network stack
items.summary: For when Refresh did not help: no internet on any app, or network adapters that are missing or stuck. Puts Windows' network settings back to their defaults.
items.effect: A fixed IP address, custom DNS servers or a manually set proxy may need to be entered again, and VPN software may need reinstalling. Needs a restart to finish.
sources: Microsoft Support: Fix network connection issues (Winsock and TCP/IP reset)

options.label: Also clear the system proxy
options.detail: Use if a proxy you do not use is blocking the connection.

items.name: Clear stuck print jobs
items.summary: For a printer that says “printing” forever, or documents that cannot be cancelled. Stops the print service, empties the print queue and starts it again.
items.effect: All waiting print jobs are cancelled. Printers and their drivers are not touched.
sources: Microsoft Support: Printer spooler troubleshooting (clear the PRINTERS folder)

items.name: Restart sound services
items.summary: For no sound, crackling, or a speaker or headset that Windows does not see. Restarts the services that run audio.
items.effect: Sound stops for a few seconds, and apps playing audio may need to be restarted.
sources: Microsoft Support: Fix sound or audio problems

options.label: Also restart Bluetooth support
options.detail: Bluetooth devices disconnect for a moment and reconnect by themselves.

items.name: Rescan hardware
items.summary: For a USB device, drive or dock that was plugged in but does not show up. Asks Windows to look for hardware changes, like Device Manager's Scan button.
items.effect: Nothing is removed or changed; devices Windows finds are set up as usual.

items.name: Reset Microsoft Store
items.summary: For a Store that will not open, loads forever, or fails to download or update apps.
items.effect: Clears the Store's cache. You stay signed in and keep your apps. The Store opens by itself when the reset finishes. Windows requires administrator permission for this tool.
sources: Microsoft Support: Reset the Microsoft Store cache (WSReset)

items.name: Fix Start menu and taskbar
items.summary: For a Start menu or search box that will not open, a blank or frozen taskbar, or a Settings app that closes at once. Registers Windows' own shell apps again.
items.effect: The taskbar disappears for a few seconds while File Explorer restarts. Your pinned items and settings are kept.
sources: Microsoft Q&A: Start menu not working (re-register the shell packages)

steps.title: Register the Start menu, taskbar and Settings apps again
args: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; $hosts = 'ShellExperienceHost', 'StartMenuExperienceHost', 'SearchApp', 'SearchUI', 'SearchHost', 'SystemSettings'; $failed = @(); foreach ($name in 'Microsoft.Windows.ShellExperienceHost', 'Microsoft.Windows.StartMenuExperienceHost', 'windows.immersivecontrolpanel') { $packages = @(Get-AppxPackage -Name $name | Where-Object { $_ }); if ($packages.Count -eq 0) { "$name is not installed."; continue }; foreach ($package in $packages) { $manifest = Join-Path $package.InstallLocation 'AppXManifest.xml'; $done = $false; $reason = ''; foreach ($attempt in 1, 2) { try { Add-AppxPackage -DisableDevelopmentMode -ForceApplicationShutdown -Register $manifest; $done = $true; break } catch { $reason = $_.Exception.Message.Split([char]10)[0].Trim(); if ($attempt -eq 1) { "$name is in use. Closing it so Windows can open it again, then trying once more."; Get-Process -Name $hosts -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Start-Sleep -Seconds 3 } } }; if ($done) { "Registered $name." } else { $failed += $name; "Could not register $name. $reason" } } }; if ($failed.Count -gt 0) { throw ('Could not register: ' + (($failed | Select-Object -Unique) -join ', ') + '. Restart Windows and run this fix again.') }

items.name: Fix wrong or blank icons
items.summary: For icons that show the wrong picture, a plain white page, or thumbnails that never appear. Deletes the saved icon pictures so Windows draws them fresh.
items.effect: The taskbar and desktop disappear for a few seconds, and folders may be slow to show thumbnails the first time afterwards.
sources: Microsoft Q&A: Rebuild the icon cache

steps.title: Delete the saved icons and thumbnails

items.name: Reset OneDrive
items.summary: For OneDrive that is stuck syncing, shows the wrong status, or will not start. Resets the sync app without touching your files.
items.effect: OneDrive restarts by itself within a minute or two (open it from Start if it does not) and checks all its files again, which can take a while. No files are deleted.
items.duration: A minute, then OneDrive syncs again
